svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.8.7.7 Design and Attachment of Handrails
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.8.7.7 Design and Attachment of Handrails
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.8 STAIRS, RAMPS, LANDINGS, HANDRAILS AND GUARDS
Design and Attachment of Handrails
WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Handrails and their supports withstand these
loads, which need not act together
(a) a concentrated load of not less than 0.9 kN
(202 lbf) applied at any point and in any
direction, for all handrails, and (b) for
handrails other than those serving a single
dwelling unit, a uniform load of not less than
0.7 kN/m (48 lbf/ft).
Single dwelling unit or house with a secondary
suite, attached to wood studs or blocking:
deemed to comply where
(a) attachment points are not more than 1.2 m
(3′-11¼″) apart on the horizontal, (b) the first
point at each end is not more than 300 mm (11
13/16″) from the end of the handrail, and (c)
each point has at least 2 No. 8 wood screws
penetrating not less than 32 mm (1¼″) into solid
wood.
Why
Handrails guide, support and arrest falls, so
loads can be considerable. In a single dwelling
unit, attachment may be accepted on experience or
structural design.
Drawn: a level length of handrail on a stud wall, finish shown see-through. Arrows show the two load cases.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.8.7.7. (page 9-37), with Note A-9.8.7.7.
